app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: Insufficient conclusive evidence to localize the failure to a single component. The cluster shows a clear symptom (ECONNREFUSED when frontend-proxy connects to the shipping Service ClusterIP 10.96.152.30:8080) while the shipping pod (shipping-68f877fd46-lgsfm, 10.244.1.38) is healthy and listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and Envoy/frontend-proxy is configured to call 10.96.152.30:8080. The most likely root cause is a node-level network translation or filtering issue (DNAT/iptables rules managed by kube-proxy, or host firewall) causing connections to the ClusterIP to be rejected. However, kube-proxy’s DaemonSet and pod on the node appear Running and showed no obvious errors in describe output, and we did not capture iptables NAT rules or an in-cluster curl/telnet comparison to definitively prove DNAT/misprogrammed iptables as the failure point. Therefore we cannot conclusively localize the root cause without performing the remaining targeted checks (see tasks_to_be_executed).

final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Traces from frontend-proxy show ECONNREFUSED connecting to 10.96.152.30:8080. 2) kubectl describe svc shipping shows ClusterIP 10.96.152.30:8080 with Ready endpoint 10.244.1.38:8080 (targetRef shipping-68f877fd46-lgsfm). 3) shipping pod logs show the service bound to addr="0.0.0.0:8080" and continuous Requesting/Sending Quote activity, with Ready=True and RestartCount=0. 4) Envoy in frontend-proxy started and initialized clusters and is configured to use port 8080, so there is no evidence of a service/port mismatch. 5) kube-proxy DaemonSet pod exists and was Running/Ready with no describe-time events indicating iptables programming failures, but iptables NAT rules were not inspected and no node-local curl/iptables checks were performed. These items together detect a real anomaly (ClusterIP refused) and point to the node-level DNAT/iptables or host-network filtering as the most likely failure surface but lack the definitive rule-level proof.
final_report.investigation_summary: Investigations prioritized platform/network (priority 1) and dependency/config (priority 2), followed by Service->Endpoint mapping (priority 3) and application health (priority 4). Steps performed: svc/endpoints/pod/DaemonSet/ConfigMap inspections; shipping pod logs review; frontend-proxy/Envoy logs review; kube-proxy pod describe. Findings: Service->Endpoint->Pod mapping is correct; shipping pod is healthy and listening on 0.0.0.0:8080; Envoy is configured to call the ClusterIP:8080 seen in traces; kube-proxy pod is Running on the node hosting the shipping pod and had no evident events. Conflicting interpretations arose: priority-1 checks discounted kube-proxy failure based on daemon/pod health and lack of kube-proxy errors, while priority-3 reasoning (correct iptables mode + correct mapping + ClusterIP refusal) pointed to kube-proxy/iptables or host firewall as the failure point. The investigation did not include the decisive tests (in-cluster curl from frontend-proxy/debug pod to ClusterIP vs Pod IP and inspection of iptables -t nat rules on the node), so we cannot conclusively prove or disprove DNAT/iptables as root cause.
